## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

BENCH|fps=19.6 proc=44.5 phys=5.4 draw=3346 prim=870361
BENCH|merged=true hidden_vis=0 walls=712
BENCH|merged_surfaces=1 verts=533320

Results:
- FPS 18.2 → 19.6 (+7.7%)
- proc 46.4 → 44.5ms
- draw 3391 → 3346 (only −45?! expected ~−470)
- prim 435k → **870k** (doubled because merged mesh always drawn, no culling)

Draw calls didn't drop as expected. Why? Perhaps culling: individual walls were already frustum-culled; hidden count shows `hidden_vis=0`?? My hidden detection wrong (visual node is child `vis` of Wall; hidden_vis counts non-MeshInstance Node3D children not visible → but we set `mi.visible=false` on the MeshInstance inside vis, not vis itself). So hidden=0 expected; check differently. Merged exists with 533,320 verts (712 walls? at merge time ~? 533k verts vs probe's 472→428k; 533k implies ~570 walls included? Hmm timers).

Draw calls barely changed: maybe walls individually were mostly culled before (only ~50-100 visible), so removing them saved few draws, while merged always draws 533k verts → primitives doubled, GPU cost up. Net +1.4 FPS (measured under contention).

So wall merging: modest +7%, increases GPU vertex load (870k prim always). Tradeoff: on low-end mobile GPU, always drawing 533k verts may hurt. Hmm risky. But FPS measured 19.6 vs 18.2, keep? Memory +533k verts in one mesh (maybe ~10-20MB). Acceptable but visual? Fine.

However primitives 870k and always full wall mesh could be significantly worse when camera looks away? Frustum culling removed; GPU still processes vertex shader for 533k verts every frame (~unavoidable). Compared to 18.2 baseline, net positive measured.

But draw call drop small means bottleneck is elsewhere? proc 44.5ms still. Let's think: headless after fixes? collision 0.16 → headless FPS likely ~89 (frame 11ms). extends StaticBody3D

const DecorMesh = preload("res://scripts/entities/DecorMesh.gd")

# 高规格墙体标记（高地外周墙用）：由 BattleManager._add_wall 在加入场景前设置
var hq: bool = false
# 外周连续城墙：端面平齐的 2m 墙段，相邻段无缝拼接
var outer: bool = false
var outer_len: float = 2.0

func _ready():
	# 程序化石墙模型（替代原 wall.glb）：按坐标哈希取种子，镜像对称仍然成立
	var seed_v: int = int(round(absf(position.x) * 10.0)) * 37 + int(round(absf(position.z) * 10.0)) * 91
	var vis: Node3D
	if outer:
		vis = DecorMesh.outer_wall_visual(outer_len)
	elif hq:
		vis = DecorMesh.wall_visual_hq(seed_v)
	else:
		vis = DecorMesh.wall_visual(seed_v)
	add_child(vis)
	# 墙体为静态装饰：不投影（阴影 pass 里 700+ 墙段是主要 draw call 负担）
	_set_shadow_off(vis)

	# 碰撞形状
	var col = CollisionShape3D.new()
	col.shape = BoxShape3D.new()
	col.shape.size = Vector3(0.4, 3, 0.4)
	add_child(col)
	add_to_group("walls")
	# 设置碰撞层
	collision_layer = 1
	collision_mask = 0

func _set_shadow_off(n: Node) -> void:
	if n is MeshInstance3D:
		(n as MeshInstance3D).cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
	for c in n.get_children():
		_set_shadow_off(c)

Minimap already: terrain pre-rendered texture; but per frame draws 712 static walls (one draw call each? `MinimapDraw.draw_wall` probably `draw_rect`/polygon per wall → 712 draws) and bushes (~hundreds) each frame, despite being static (`_static_walls`, `_static_bushes` arrays).

Fix: pre-render static bushes+walls into the terrain texture (or a second static texture drawn once as one draw), so per-frame draws drop by ~1000+. Dynamic parts (turrets 20, minions clusters 2, jungle 20, heroes 10, health packs 54, viewport, fog, objectives) remain ~150 draws.

Implementation: extend `_ensure_terrain_texture` / `_cache_static_map` to build an **ImageTexture** containing walls+bushes (plus existing terrain) once. But MinimapDraw.draw_bush/draw_wall draw onto a CanvasItem; can't draw into Image directly. Options:
- Use `SubViewport` rendering once: create SubViewport (300×300, transparent bg), add Node2D with custom _draw calling MinimapDraw.draw_bush/draw_wall using local coords, then capture `viewport.get_texture().get_image()` and create ImageTexture. One-time cost ~ cheap. Complexity moderate (need await frame_post_draw; but minimap already may render terrain image manually).
- Or approximate with Image drawing: walls = 2.5px squares; bushes = dots; draw via Image.fill_rect per pixel rect (712+~400 = 1100 fill_rect on 300×300 image, one-time ~ms). Visual approximation of draw_wall's polygon shape (walls are thin rotated rects; use 2px rect ignoring rotation) may be acceptable but could look slightly different.

Check how `_cache_static_map` currently collects, and `_ensure_terrain_texture`; read Minimap.gd lines 34-80, 219-235, 375-445. Read file sections.

static func draw_bush(ci: CanvasItem, pos: Vector2, r: float = 3.4) -> void:
	ci.draw_circle(pos, r * 1.5, Color(0.28, 0.62, 0.32, 0.16))
	ci.draw_circle(pos, r, Color(0.10, 0.30, 0.16, 0.85))
	ci.draw_arc(pos, r, 0, TAU, 14, Color(0.34, 0.78, 0.40, 0.55), 1.0)
	for i in range(3):
		var a: float = TAU * float(i) / 3.0 + 0.5
		ci.draw_line(pos, pos + Vector2(cos(a), sin(a)) * r * 0.72, Color(0.42, 0.86, 0.48, 0.45), 1.0)

## 墙体：旋转长条 + 影子 + 顶部高光
static func draw_wall(ci: CanvasItem, pos: Vector2, ang: float, length: float = 5.0, thick: float = 2.6) -> void:
	var d := Vector2(cos(ang), sin(ang))
	var p := Vector2(-d.y, d.x)
	var hl: float = length * 0.5
	var ht: float = thick * 0.5
	var quad := PackedVector2Array([pos - d * hl - p * ht, pos + d * hl - p * ht, pos + d * hl + p * ht, pos - d * hl + p * ht])

(a) generate a separate `_static_overlay_texture` and draw it (1 extra draw call), or
(b) merge into terrain image before creating texture — need access to the Image: modify MinimapDraw.terrain_texture? Better do (a): create Image(256,256, transparent), paint walls/bushes with pixel coords scaled 256/120 = 2.133 px/m; wall length 1.8m*2.133=3.84px, thick 2.35px; bushes radius 3m*2.133=6.4px (in 256 space). Then draw_texture_rect stretched to MINIMAP_SIZE — same look as before (since current drawing uses MINIMAP_SIZE scale = 300/120=2.5; with 256 texture stretched to 300 it's equivalent scale).

But texture resolution 256 vs minimap 300 → slightly blurrier; acceptable or use 300 (MINIMAP_SIZE). Use `int(MINIMAP_SIZE)` size for 1:1 pixels; but texture baked before size known? MINIMAP_SIZE set before _ready (BattleManager sets 300 before adding). Fine, create at MINIMAP_SIZE.

Paint helpers:
```gdscript
func _paint_static_overlay() -> ImageTexture:
	var size_px := int(MINIMAP_SIZE)
	var img := Image.create(size_px, size_px, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
	img.fill(Color(0,0,0,0))
	var k := float(size_px) / float(MAP_SIZE)  # px per meter
	# 草丛
	for b in _static_bushes:
		_paint_disc(img, b * (size_px / MINIMAP_SIZE)?)
```
Careful: `_static_bushes` coords are in minimap pixel space (MINIMAP_SIZE units). We want texture pixel space = size_px = MINIMAP_SIZE → same coordinate space! Since MINIMAP_SIZE is int 300, target texture 300×300 → coords identical. 

So bake at size = MINIMAP_SIZE, coords unchanged: bush radius `3.0 * MINIMAP_SIZE/MAP_SIZE`=7.5; wall length 1.8*2.5=4.5, thick 1.1*2.5=2.75.

Disc paint with alpha blend:
```gdscript
func _paint_disc(img: Image, c: Vector2, r: float, col: Color) -> void:
	var r2 := r * r
	for y in range(int(floor(c.y - r)), int(ceil(c.y + r)) + 1):
		if y < 0 or y >= img.get_height(): continue
		for x in range(int(floor(c.x - r)), int(ceil(c.x + r)) + 1):
			if x < 0 or x >= img.get_width(): continue
			var dx := float(x) + 0.5 - c.x
			var dy := float(y) + 0.5 - c.y
			if dx*dx + dy*dy <= r2:
				_blend_px(img, x, y, col)
```
wall as rotated quad fill: sample along length steps (length/half-thick):
```gdscript
func _paint_wall_quad(img: Image, pos: Vector2, ang: float, length: float, thick: float, col: Color) -> void:
	var d := Vector2(cos(ang), sin(ang))
	var p := Vector2(-d.y, d.x)
	var hl := length * 0.5
	var ht := thick * 0.5
	var steps := int(maxf(ceil(length * 2.0), 2.0))
	for i in range(steps + 1):
		var t := -hl + length * float(i) / float(steps)
		var base := pos + d * t
		var tsteps := int(maxf(ceil(thick * 2.0), 1.0))
		for j in range(tsteps + 1):
			var o := -ht + thick * float(j) / float(tsteps)
			var q := base + p * o
			_paint_px(img, int(round(q.x)), int(round(q.y)), col)
```
Blend:
```gdscript
func _blend_px(img: Image, x: int, y: int, col: Color) -> void:
	if x < 0 or y < 0 or x >= img.get_width() or y >= img.get_height(): return
	var dst: Color = img.get_pixel(x, y)
	var a: float = col.a
	if dst.a > 0.0:
		var out_a: float = a + dst.a * (1.0 - a)
		col = Color((col.r*a + dst.r*dst.a*(1.0-a))/out_a, ..., out_a)
	img.set_pixel(x, y, col)
```

Parse clean (known warning), smoke 0 errors, probes cleaned, notified.

Final report:
- Overall: 12.5 → 43.8 FPS (3.5×), frame 80ms → 23ms.
- Changes list with metrics per step:
  1. CollisionSystem spatial grid: 14ms → 0.16ms.
  2. Wall shadow off (712), shadow 3072→2048, max distance 60, MSAA off: 12.5→18.2.
  3. Wall mesh merge experiment tested, reverted (draw calls barely changed, primitives doubled).
  4. Minimap static bake: main win, 20.5 → 43.8 FPS, draws 3420 → 1138; minimap alone was ~2500 draws/frame (712 walls × 4 draws + 84 bushes × ~7).
- Verification: parse 0 errors, 600-frame smoke 0 SCRIPT ERROR; screenshot saved.
- Remaining: ~1100 draws (UI ~600, minimap dynamic ~300, 3D ~200 at hidden test). FPS capped by vsync 60? Actually 43.8 below.

Also note the caveat: machine had other agents' instances; final numbers measured while ~1 game instance.

Files linked: CollisionSystem.gd, Wall.gd, project.godot, Minimap.gd. Also mention screenshots `screenshots/minimap_fixed.png`.

Keep concise, conclusion first.

**帧率从 12.5 提升到 43.8 FPS（约 3.5 倍），帧耗时从 80ms 降到 23ms。** 最大的性能瓶颈已经找到：小地图每帧都在重画静态地形——712 段墙体（每段 4 次 draw 调用）加 84 处草丛，合计约 **3000 个 draw call**。

**本轮改动**
1. **小地图静态元素烘焙为贴图**（[Minimap.gd:224](scripts/ui/Minimap.gd#L224)）：把草丛、墙体的影子、填充和描边一次性画进一张 300×300 透明 `ImageTexture`，之后每帧只绘制 1 张图；动态部分（英雄、塔、小兵、血包、迷雾、视野框）保持不变。
2. **CollisionSystem 空间网格**（[CollisionSystem.gd:4](scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd#L4)）：每个实体只检查周围 3×3 格墙体，代替原来「50 实体 × 712 墙」的全量遍历。
3. **墙体不再投射阴影**（[Wall.gd:12](scripts/entities/Wall.gd#L12)）：712 段城墙视觉 `cast_shadow=OFF`。
4. **渲染设置降档**（[project.godot:139](project.godot#L139)）：方向光阴影 3072→2048、阴影距离 60、MSAA 3D 关闭。

**验证数据**

| 指标 | 优化前 | 优化后 |
|---|---|---|
| FPS（2400×1400 窗口） | 12.5 | **43.8** |
| TIME_PROCESS | 64–68ms | **21ms** |
| Draw calls | 3650 | **1138** |
| 碰撞耗时 | 12.6–14ms | **0.16ms** |
| headless FPS | 34 | **89** |

- 解析 0 错（仅已知 Minimap 警告）；战斗 600 帧 smoke 0 SCRIPT ERROR。
- 小地图检查：烘焙贴图 300×300、19,222 个不透明像素（墙体约 3,660），截图 [minimap_fixed.png](screenshots/minimap_fixed.png) 中地图区域色彩层次正常。
- 顺手验证过“把 712 段墙合并成一个 Mesh”的方案，实测 draw call 只降 45、图元翻倍（合并后失去视锥剔除），已回退，未留在代码里。

**剩余瓶颈**：还剩约 1,100 个 draw call，主要是 UI 常规绘制（约 600）、小地图动态元素（约 300）以及 3D 场景约 200；继续优化可以在 UI 合并批次、动态元素聚类上做，但收益已经明显变小。另外机器上有其他 Godot 实例在跑（含 FingerEmpire），多开会拉低帧率，测帧时建议只保留一个实例。

- 单兵创建成本：窗口化 84.6ms/个（冷）、约 7ms/个（热缓存），headless 仅 2.7ms/个 → 主要不是游戏逻辑，而是创建节点时同步生成程序化模型 + 材质/管线资源（GPU 侧）导致主线程阻塞。

Fix proposal:
1. 分帧生成：把一波 20 个小兵放进队列，每帧生成 2 个（约 10 帧内完成，延迟 <0.2s），单帧峰值 140ms→~15ms；野怪/炮车/史诗怪同样处理。
2. 加载页预热：开局前在加载界面（不可见/屏幕外）先创建每种小兵/野怪各 1 个再释放，把模型与材质管线预编译，消除冷启动首波 2.5s 卡顿。
3. （可选）让小兵模型/材质按（兵种, 阵营）共享缓存，而不是每个实例重新生成。

找到了，卡顿的原因源于**“成批生成”的时机**，并非渲染帧率问题。

**实测 120 秒窗口化运行中的慢帧记录**

| 游戏时间 | 单帧耗时 | 当时发生的事 |
|---|---|---|
| 30.0s | 123ms | 野怪营地首次刷新 |
| 33.1s | 138ms | 兵线刷新，同帧 minions +20 |
| 66.1s | 138ms | 兵线刷新，同帧 minions +20 |
| 99.1s | 145ms | 兵线刷新，同帧 minions +20 |
| 105.9s | 138ms | 战斗杂项 |

**根因：整波小兵在同一个帧里一次性生成**
- `_process` 中的 `minion_spawn_timer <= 0` 每 33 秒触发一次 `_spawn_minion_wave()`（[BattleManager.gd:4428](scripts/core/BattleManager.gd#L4428)），而它会在一个帧内连续创建 20 个小兵（[BattleManager.gd:4764](scripts/core/BattleManager.gd#L4764) 的循环与 `spawn_single_minion`）。
- 单个小兵的创建成本（窗口化实测）：**84.6ms/个（冷缓存）、约 7ms/个（热缓存）**；同样代码 headless 只要 **2.7ms/个**。也就是说，几乎全部耗时都花在“创建可视化节点时同步生成程序化模型，并创建材质和管线”上；游戏逻辑本身并不慢。
- 20 个 × 7ms ≈ 140ms，正好对应每次兵线造成的“一顿”。冷启动后的第一波更严重：直接计时 `_spawn_minion_wave()` 实测 **2554ms**（每个小兵约 128ms，包含管线编译），这就是开局第一次兵线或第一次刷野时“大顿一下”的原因。
- 30 秒那次 123ms 同理：`_update_pending_jungle_spawns` 一次性生成多个野怪营地。4 分钟炮车波、史诗野怪刷新也会重复同样的模式。

**修复建议（两个小改动即可）**
1. **分帧生成**：把一波小兵进入生成队列，每帧只创建 1–2 个（10 帧内完成，实际出场延迟 <0.2s），单帧峰值 140ms → 约 15ms；野怪、炮车、史诗怪同样排队。
2. **加载页预热**：开局前在屏幕外先各创建 1 个兵种/野怪原型再释放，提前完成模型与管线的创建，消除冷启动首波的 2.5s 卡顿。
3. 进一步可做：小兵模型/材质按（兵种、阵营）共享缓存，避免每个实例重复生成。

要我直接按 1+2 动手吗？改完我会用同一套 120 秒的帧耗时采样来复测验证。

要

Implement fixes 1+2:

1. Frame-sliced spawn queue for minion wave (and jungle/epic spawns? user said 1+2; fix 1 mentions waves, jungle, siege, epic; but keep scope minimal: minion waves + jungle pending spawns are main measured. Epic monsters at 235s maybe also; check `_update_epic_monsters`).

2. Prewarm at loading screen: create one prototype of each minion type (and jungle monsters?) offscreen and free, so procedural meshes/materials/pipelines compiled. Where? In `_start_game` loading flow or `_start_game_body`? Loading screen exists (`_start_game` shows loading UI then loads). Prewarm uses `_create_visual` only — build objects, don't need actual game entities? Simpler: instantiate `Minion.new()` with proper display_name/team, set visible=false, position far offscreen, add_child then `queue_free()` after a frame. But pipeline compile happens at first *render* of that mesh; if invisible, it won't render → no compile. Need to render it: place far away offscreen? Offscreen = culled → no compile either. Better place near camera but behind UI (hidden by loading screen overlay) — during loading screen, camera at base; put prototype at hero position with scale small; render one frame, then free.

Alternative: use `RenderingServer`? Simplest: spawn prototypes visible for a few frames during the loading screen (loading UI covers screen) then free. The loading screen in `_start_game` likely covers full screen with art, so visuals hidden behind UI. Implement in `_start_game_body` after loading finishes? At that point loading screen hidden... 

Maybe warm earlier: in `_ready`/`_create_map` no. Best place: `_start_game` shows loading; find where loading finishes then hide; prewarm during loading stage: create prototypes as children near camera; loading UI on top (CanvasLayer above 3D) so hidden.

Note `_start_game_body` calls `GameEntity.debug_show_path = true` — that enables A* debug path visual for ALL AI heroes! Debug path visuals each frame could cause overhead & maybe hitches (path spheres). That's a debug leftover; likely unrelated to periodic hitch but adds per-frame cost. Could mention/disable? Not in scope (user wants hitches fixed). Might be a separate perf issue; ignore for now (or note).

Loading screen stays visible during `_start_game_body`? `_on_loading_finished` sets loading_screen=null then calls body — loading UI probably freed when finished signal emits (after 2.8s). So during `_start_game_body`, loading screen may be gone → prewarm prototypes would be visible. But loading finished → game starts immediately; we can prewarm prototypes and free them **within the same frame**, they may render? No render occurs until frame ends; if freed same frame, never rendered. Need them rendered ~2-3 frames.

Alternative prewarm location: during `_start_game` (before loading screen shown/completes) — at line 312-315, the map/heroes don't exist yet (create entities in `_start_game_body`), but prewarm only needs prototypes independent of map: create Minion nodes as children of bm with `visible=true`, positioned in front of camera (cam exists from `_ready` at map center though hero not created; camera at (0,20,10) initial), then free after few frames — during loading screen (2.8s), the loading UI covers screen (CanvasLayer full-rect), so 3D visible behind UI but hidden. That works: schedule prewarm right when `_start_game` shows loading (line 315) and free prototypes after e.g. 0.5s via timer.

But careful: creating Minion nodes during loading adds them to "minions" group; AI/vision may see them; they'd be removed after 0.5s. Also they might affect gameplay if not removed. Use team NEUTRAL? Minion team 2 → enemy vision? We can set health/max and then queue_free quickly; but they could be targeted/attacked during 0.5s (heroes created only in `_start_game_body`, later). Safe.

Alternatively prewarm without adding as real entities: create `Minion.new()` nodes but don't call `_start_game_body` logic; just `add_child` them at a far location visible? Camera at (0,20,10) looking -60°: place at (0,0,0) near camera view; loading UI covers. They'll be in minions group briefly.

Which prototypes: minion types: melee, ranged, siege, super, dragon, storm? `spawn_single_minion(type...)` supports melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon/storm. MinionModel.is_applied(display_name) determines procedural vs GLB models. display_name mapping in spawn_single_minion — check lines 4826-4900 to know names & team.

Also jungle monsters: `_create_jungle` spawns camps at 30s? pending spawns create JungleMonster types; prewarming all monster types could be many. Keep prewarm: 6 minion types × 2 teams? Materials tint per team (UnitVisuals.tint_team duplicates materials) → need both teams. 12 prototypes ~ 12×(84ms cold) ≈ 1s during loading (2.8s) — acceptable! But if prototypes created all same frame, that frame takes 1s, loading screen anim may hitch but it's loading. Better spawn prewarm prototypes across frames using same frame-sliced queue? Simpler: prewarm on a timer, one prototype per frame during loading (create, wait frame, free). Over 2.8s at 60fps = 168 frames, plenty.

But wait: cold cost is largely pipeline compile at first render; invisible prototypes won't compile. Need visible in camera view. During loading screen, the 3D scene behind is rendered? LoadingScreen likely CanvasLayer with solid background → 3D still rendered (behind), so visible prototypes render → compile ✓.

Also note `_start_game_body` sets `GameEntity.debug_show_path=true` — irrelevant.

Implementation plan:
A. Frame-sliced minion spawning:
- Add `var _pending_minion_spawns: Array = []`, `var _minion_spawn_budget := 2` (per frame).
- `_spawn_minion_wave()`: instead of calling `spawn_single_minion` directly, append call args to queue. But wave logic includes dragon_count, siege decisions; produce list of [type, team, pos, line, lane_idx] tuples then queue.
- In `_process`, after `_spawn_minion_wave` trigger, drain queue: `while not _pending_minion_spawns.is_empty() and spawned < 2: spawn_single_minion(...)`.
- Same-frame visual appearance trick: minions appear 10 frames later (~0.17s) — acceptable.
- Also drain starving: if queue large (e.g., >40), allow 3/frame.

B. Prewarm at loading:
- In `_start_game`, after `add_child(loading_screen)`: `_prewarm_match_assets()` (a coroutine using `await` frames), creating one prototype per (minion type × 2 teams) at camera front, visible, then freeing after 2 frames.
- Types list: "melee","ranged","siege","super","dragon","storm" maybe plus jungle monster types? Jungle spawn is at 30s (123ms hitch) — user's fix 1 mentions jungle too; frame-slicing jungle spawn at 30s also helps but prewarm jungle models would remove per-instance compile. Could prewarm jungle monsters too — need know types created in `_update_pending_jungle_spawns` (JungleMonster.new with display_name). Could prewarm JungleMonster via same method? Let me check spawn code for pending jungle. Might be simpler: frame-slice pending jungle spawns too (drain 1/frame) → 123ms→~40ms each.

Let me inspect `_update_pending_jungle_spawns` and `spawn_single_minion` names.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Long-running HonorKing polish project (Honor of Kings–style 3D MOBA, Godot 4.7.2, GDScript, mobile renderer). Many earlier batches shipped (feel P0, UI parity, BP, loading screen, hero skill FX, HUD layout, hit-impact FX).
- Prior request: “现在的平均帧率为10左右，请你分析主要性能瓶颈在哪里” → analysis delivered.
- Then: “直接动手吧” → implemented performance P1 (collision spatial grid, wall shadows off, shadow/MSAA downgrade): 12.5 → 18.2 FPS.
- Then: “继续” → tested/experimented; wall-mesh merge reverted (no gain, primitives doubled); delivered the biggest win in the minimap (static bushes/walls baked to a texture): 12.5 → **43.8 FPS**, draw calls 3650 → 1138.
- Current request (verbatim): “虽然帧率不低，但是没过一段时间画面就会一顿，请你找出原因” — i.e. intermittent periodic frame hitches/stutters, despite decent average FPS; find the cause (diagnosis priority).

## Key Technical Concepts
- Godot 4.7.2, `rendering_method="mobile"`, window 2400×1400, `stretch/mode="canvas_items"`, vsync_mode=2.
- Profiling via `Performance.get_monitor(TIME_PROCESS / TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS / RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME / RENDER_TOTAL_PRIMITIVES_IN_FRAME)`, `Engine.get_frames_per_second()`, `Time.get_ticks_usec()`, frame `delta * 1000` for hitch detection.
- Godot runtime pipeline cache in `C:\Users\18749\AppData\Roaming\Godot\app_userdata\HonorKing\shader_cache`; project cache `.godot/shader_cache` (3.0 MB).
- Minion wave interval 33.0 s (`minion_spawn_timer` reset in `_process`); delayed jungle spawns at 30 s/60 s; epic monsters 235 s; team tactics every 60 s after 240 s; MVP recompute every 30 s; stats every 1 s.
- Minion visual creation: `Minion._ready()` → `_create_visual()` → `MinionModelScript.build(display_name, team)` + `UnitVisuals.tint_team` + `WalkFeel.attach` (procedural model + materials).
- A* pathfinding: `GameEntity._avoid_walls()` calls `PathFinder.find_path(...)` when `desired` moves >2 m or path empty; `debug_show_path` static = false.
- Verification: `--headless --editor --quit` parse check; headless smoke `--quit-after 600`; windowed probe scenes `_probe_*.gd/.tscn` (delete afterwards incl. `.uid`); screenshots saved via `get_viewport().get_texture().get_image().save_png()` after `await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw`.
- Godot binary: `D:\Downloads\06_游戏与Flash资源\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe`; workspace `C:\Users\18749\Documents\honor-king`.
- Known-benign: `Class "Minimap" hides a global script class` + `Failed to load script "res://scripts/ui/MiniMap.gd"`; `user://` log-open errors.
- Machine shared with other active agents/sessions (concurrent Godot instances, mid-edit files) → noise, transient parse errors, hangs.

## Files and Code
- `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` (rewritten): wall spatial hash `WALL_CELL := 4.0`, `_wall_pts`, `_wall_grid`, `_rebuild_wall_grid()`, entity-pair filtering (skip Turret/Hero), 3×3 cell wall query; collision 12.6–14 ms → **0.14–0.16 ms**.
- `scripts/entities/Wall.gd`: `_set_shadow_off(vis)` recursive, all wall MeshInstances `cast_shadow = SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF`; wall merge experiment added then fully reverted (file now 40 lines, no static vars/merge funcs).
- `project.godot` lines ~139–141: `lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/size=2048`, `lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/max_distance=60.0`, `anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_3d=0` (was 3072/2).
- `scripts/ui/Minimap.gd`: added `var _static_overlay_texture: ImageTexture = null`; `_draw()` now calls `_cache_static_map()` then `_bake_static_overlay()` once and draws 1 texture instead of per-frame loops over `_static_bushes` (84) + `_static_walls` (472, each 4 draws); new helpers `_bake_static_overlay()`, `_paint_disc()`, `_paint_wall_quad()`, `_blend_pixel()`; bake at `int(MINIMAP_SIZE)` (300×300), 19,222 opaque px, wall-like 3,660.
- `scripts/ui/MinimapDraw.gd`: `draw_bush` (2 circles + arc + 3 spokes), `draw_wall` (shadow polygon + fill + polyline + highlight = 4 draws), `draw_fog` (≤144 `draw_rect`), `terrain_texture()`, `fog_grid()`.
- `scripts/core/BattleManager.gd`: `_process` at line 4329; `stats_timer` block 4394–4407 (`_update_team_stats`, `_apply_natural_experience/gold`, minute gold history); `_update_pending_jungle_spawns()` 4410; `_refresh_mvp()` 4412–4415; `_update_shadow_paths` 4416; team tactics 4418–4424 (`print("[BattleManager] t=... 执行团队分路分配")`); `_update_epic_monsters` 4426–4427; `minion_spawn_timer` 4428–4431 (`_spawn_minion_wave()`, interval 33.0); `_update_vision`, `ui.update(self)`, minimap group queries; `_update_team_stats()` def at 4186; `_spawn_minion_wave()` at 4764 (20 minions per wave: 3 lanes × both teams); `spawn_single_minion` at 4826; `_add_wall` ~2247; `minion_spawn_timer` declared line 115 = 0.0; `_pending_jungle_spawns` line 62 / spawn logic 1181–1193.
- `scripts/entities/Minion.gd`: `_ready()` line 16 → `_create_visual()` (line 26) uses `MinionModelScript.is_applied` → `MinionModelScript.build()`, else GLB `res://model/melee/soldier.glb` etc.
- `scripts/entities/GameEntity.gd`: `_avoid_walls` 1040; path recompute 1085–1103; A* debug print 1099–1102; `debug_show_path` static false (line 46); `find_path` call site 1089.
- `scripts/core/PostFX.gd`: single `ShaderMaterial` with preloaded `res://scripts/core/postfx.gdshader`; `_process` sets uniforms.
- `scripts/core/VfxFactory.gd`: creates `StandardMaterial3D` per effect (`_add_mat` line 481), `ShaderMaterial` line 272, beam/glow shaders preloaded lines 69–70.
- `scripts/core/PathFinder.gd`: `build_navigation_map()` 21, `find_path()` 122, `_mark_solid` 111, `_world_to_cell` 203; only called at map creation (BattleManager 287, 365) and from GameEntity.
- `screenshots/minimap_fixed.png`, `screenshots/minimap_overlay.png`: minimap verification artifacts (kept).

## Errors and Fixes
- Initially measured 12.5 FPS with proc 64–68 ms; found 40+ leftover Godot instances consuming ~10 cores; killed them.
- “Hide UI no change” conclusion from earlier batch was wrong/noisy; later controlled test showed UI ≈ 2700 draw calls (baseline 3413 → 679 with UI hidden, FPS 20.5 → 32.8).
- Wall-mesh merge (SurfaceTool bake of 712 walls into 1 mesh) test: FPS 18.2 → 19.6 but draw calls only −45 and primitives 435k → 870k; reverted (worse on GPU-bound devices).
- Transient parse errors while other agents save: `Identifier "_sfx" not declared`, `Identifier "_sfx_next" not declared`, `Function "_apply_layer_bands" has the same name as a previously declared function`, `Could not resolve class "GameEntity"`, `Could not parse global class "UI_Manager"`, `Attempt to call function '_start_game_body' in base 'null instance'` — external concurrent edits; parse returned clean later; do not “fix”.
- Probe with full tree walk / wave spawn against broken UI_Manager hung >180 s → moved to background job `pwsh-7823f3648f4645ec`, killed.
- A probe using `Minion.new()` and `bm._spawn_minion_wave()` failed due to above mid-edit broken repo; rerun after parse recovery needed.
- `read_image` unavailable for this model → screenshots validated numerically (Pillow / System.Drawing pixel stats; minimap crop had 502 distinct sampled colors).

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

64: 	root.set_meta("minion_model_kind", kind)
65: 	root.set_meta("tint_strength", 0.30)
66: 	return root

So minions DO call `MinionModelScript.build`. Then why wave 138ms for 20 minions (~7ms each)? Because `build` in the battle context was fast?? Our probe in battle scene measured `MinionModel.build("melee",0)` at 140-295ms at f=120 **after game start**... hmm.

Wait, maybe in battle scene probe, at f=120, `_start_game_body` was called but the **engine was still compiling renderer pipelines / GPU was busy with loading**, making wall time inflated? Yet the wave spikes 138ms for 20 spawns = 7ms each, which contradicts 140ms per build... unless the wave in that run occurred while `minion_spawn_timer` triggered... 20 minions × 7ms = 140ms. If each build were 140ms, wave would be 2.8s — we saw 2.5s in the *cold* manual wave test! Right: cold manual `_spawn_minion_wave` = 2554ms → 128ms/minion. So in the **cold/manual** case build ≈128ms; in the periodic wave (warm, real match), 7ms/minion.

Why would build be fast in real waves? Because... these frames are 138ms spikes for 20; but maybe only some minions are queued per frame and spike per frame ~140ms with 2 minions → 70ms each! Look at after-fix probe: every frame with +2 minions spikes 120-145ms. So per minion ~65ms in real match. And direct build call measured 140-295ms. Same order (2x). The discrepancy might be because in probe, `build` called at f=120 while... hmm 65 vs 140 factor 2.

Whatever: per-minion creation in real match costs ~65ms with rendering, which is crazy and explains "每 33 秒卡一下" AND our fix of spreading makes more frames hitch (2/frame × 65ms = 130ms) — no improvement.

Need a real fix: **cache/share the built model and materials across minions**. Instead of building a unique procedural model per minion, build once per (kind, team) and duplicate the Node3D hierarchy (duplicate shares Mesh and Material resources). Then each minion: build ~0ms after first, plus `duplicate()` cost small.

Why is build slow in windowed? Unknown internal (maybe `SurfaceTool.append_from` + StandardMaterial3D creation heavy due to renderer sync). Sharing the built model solves it regardless.

Implementation:
- In `MinionModel` add static cache: `static var _cache: Dictionary = {}` mapping "%s_%d" % [kind, team] → Node3D (template).
- `build(kind, team)` returns cached `.duplicate()` (duplicate(flags) default DUPLICATE_USE_INSTANTIATION? Node.duplicate() duplicates children, shares meshes/materials since resources shared by default: duplicate() duplicates node properties; Resources are shared references (not deep copied) unless DUPLICATE_USE_INSTANTIATION). So duplicate is fast.
- Need to ensure per-instance stuff: `WalkFeel.attach` modifies transforms/legs of the specific instance — duplicate creates own nodes but shares Mesh/Material — fine since tint applied per instance via UnitVisuals.tint_team (duplicates materials per instance, ok? that may also be expensive ~? tint_team duplicates StandardMaterial3D per mesh instance — probably cheap since materials are resource-dup).

So modify `build()`:
```
static var _template_cache: Dictionary = {}
static func build(kind: String, team: int) -> Node3D:
	var key := "%s|%d" % [kind, team]
	var tpl: Node3D = _template_cache.get(key)
	if tpl == null:
		tpl = _build_new(kind, team)
		_template_cache[key] = tpl
	return tpl.duplicate() as Node3D
```
Move existing body into `_build_new`.

But careful: `duplicate()` on Node3D with MeshInstance3D children shares ArrayMesh and materials — good (GPU resources shared). `WalkFeel` legs lookups reference node names — duplicated names preserved (Godot may rename duplicates only if same parent sibling name conflicts; our duplicate added as child of separate minion, so names preserved).

Also cache must be cleared per session? Static persists across matches; templates keep references to meshes/materials → reuse fine (no leak since same binding). Memory fine.

This should cut per-minion build to ~1-3ms. Then wave spike from 140ms → ~30ms (20×1.5ms + other).

Also our prewarm then naturally warms `_template_cache` for each kind/team during loading → first wave cheap ✓. And frame-slicing can stay (budget 2), but with caching, could revert to immediate spawn (simpler, less latency). Since building cached templates is cheap, spawn whole wave in one frame ~30-50ms — still a hitch; better keep queue with budget 4/frame (5 frames). Keep queue budget 2, fine.

Implement caching + prewarm (already). Then measure wave spikes again.

Note: `UnitVisuals.tint_team(instance, team, strength)` duplicates materials per instance — that may still cost per minion. Measure later.

Also cache templates per team — prewarm covers both teams ✓.

Let's edit MinionModel.build: rename to `_build_new` and add cache wrapper. Need read lines 1-30 for static vars placement.

scripts\core\WalkFeel.gd
6: ## dust=true 仅在 host 用（客户端不生成粒子，避免双端粒子预算翻倍）。
8: static func attach(unit: Node3D, model_root: Node3D, opts: Dictionary = {}) -> void:
35: var dust := true
36: var dust_col := Color(0.70, 0.64, 0.54)
37: var dust_size := 0.22
55: dust = bool(o.get("dust", true))
56: dust_col = o.get("dust_color", Color(0.70, 0.64, 0.54))
57: dust_size = float(o.get("dust_size", 0.22))
90: if last_step != 0 and dust:
92: _step_dust(p, 0.6)   # 停下时补一小蓬尘
115: if dust and step_cd <= 0.0:
117: _step_dust(p, f)
119: func _step_dust(pos: Vector3, f: float) -> void:
120: if not dust:
122: Vfx.footstep(pos + Vector3(0.0, 0.06, 0.0), dust_col, dust_size, clampf(f, 0.35, 1.3))

Dust is created on movement via Vfx (per step), not at attach. Minions do walk → each minion emits dust footsteps → Vfx.footstep creates particles... but that's per step, and the first wave's initial spikes at t=0.1-0.6 while minions start walking → dust particles created for 8 minions? Each `Vfx.footstep` maybe creates CPUParticles3D expensive (shader/pipeline). But that's during gameplay and periodic (each step) yet budget-limited presumably.

Hmm, the 123ms frames at t=0.1-0.6 correlate with spawn frames. Could include dust creation for newly walking minions.

User says "要" — wants me to eliminate the residual first-frame upload cost: "模型模板共享 + 材质合并（减少 surface 数）".

Task: reduce per-minion material/surface count. Currently `_commit` builds one ArrayMesh with up to 8 surfaces, each with its own StandardMaterial3D (steel, dark, bronze, gold, leather, wood, skin, black...). Per instance, 8 surfaces × materials → many draw calls and per-instance descriptor setup; tint creates surface override per surface (cached). Reducing to e.g. 2-3 materials via **vertex colors** on a single material would cut surfaces to 1: bake material color into vertex colors, use one material with `vertex_color_use_as_albedo = true`; metallic/roughness differ per material though — can approximate with a few materials (e.g., "metal" + "cloth/skin" + "glow").

Plan: in `MinionModel`, merge materials by category:
- metal (steel, bronze, gold → metallic ~0.55, roughness ~0.3): vertex color carries albedo.
- matte (dark, leather, wood, skin, cloth, black → metallic 0, roughness ~0.85): vertex color.
- emissive (eyes etc.) maybe already part of `_mat_emit` keys.

But `_mat` sets albedo colors; to bake into vertex colors, need to modify `_ensure/_box/_cyl/_sph/_limb/_tri/_append` calls to set vertex color from material key. `_append` uses `st.append_from(mesh, 0, xf)` where mesh from `_ensure`? Actually `_append(sts, mats, key, mesh, xf)` uses `st.append_from(mesh, 0, xf)` — append_from copies mesh arrays; to add vertex colors we need to set color per vertex. Approach: for each key, set a color property on the SurfaceTool before appending? SurfaceTool has `set_color()` which applies to subsequent `add_vertex` calls, but `append_from` appends an existing mesh's arrays — does it apply current color? `SurfaceTool.append_from` copies the mesh's arrays as-is, ignoring current color.

Alternative simpler approach: **post-process the committed surfaces**: after commit, merge surfaces by remapping material → use vertex colors? Need geometry with vertex color arrays.

Alternative: build separate SurfaceTools per color group, then use `SurfaceTool.append_from` won't help.

Hmm. Simpler optimization: reduce **number of distinct materials per kind**: e.g., map 9 materials to 3 (metal, matte, emissive) with fixed colors per material → still can't carry per-part albedo difference unless merged colors are compromises (visually worse). But maybe acceptable? The user asked "材质合并（减少 surface 数）" — they accept visual simplification.

But careful: `UnitVisuals.tint_team` operates per surface with `_tint_cache` keyed by material instance; fewer surfaces = less dup cost (already cached) and fewer draw calls per minion.

Better approach preserving visuals: use **vertex colors** properly by writing custom append:
- Instead of `st.append_from(mesh, 0, xf)`, extract arrays and add vertices manually with color. `SurfaceTool` supports `add_vertex` + `set_color`; for each triangle, transform vertices by xf, set normal, set color per material. We can implement `_append` replacement that gets `mesh.surface_get_arrays(0)` and pushes verts/index. That's more code but doable and keeps visuals.

Cost/benefit: this reduces surfaces per minion from 8 to 1-2 → per-instance upload/descriptor work much cheaper, draw calls down.

However time/budget: user asked to do it. Also they earlier wanted minimal diffs. Let's implement:

1. In `_materials`, return a small dict mapping material-name → color + group (metal/matte/emissive). Keep function signature; but `_ensure` uses `mats` too? `_ensure(sts, mats, key)` creates SurfaceTool per key and stores material in `mats[key]`? Let me read `_ensure`, `_append`, `_commit`, and helpers to understand key handling before editing.

Current: one SurfaceTool per material key, each with material; commit adds one surface per key → 8-9 surfaces per minion mesh, each with material. Per minion, mesh is SHARED across instances now (template duplicated shares mesh). So surfaces per mesh fixed; draw calls 8-9 per minion → 20 minions = 180 draws. Reducing surfaces helps draws & upload.

But first-frame hitch: is it per-surface? The earlier per-minion cost 65ms windowed even with shared mesh... What cost remains? Possibly `MeshInstance3D` with vertex color? Hmm. The residual 120ms spike for 2 minions might be dust VFX (`Vfx.footstep`), not the mesh at all. But the user wants material merging; deliver it.

Implement plan: **bake material albedo into vertex colors; merge into 2 surfaces: opaque (metal/matte combined with vertex color) + emissive (unchanged separate key)**.

Material groups:
- metal: steel, bronze, gold, dark? dark is metallic 0.38/rough 0.55 — could go metal.
- matte: leather, wood, skin, cloth, black, dark? 

Simplify to two: "metal" (metallic 0.5, roughness 0.35) and "matte" (metallic 0.0, roughness 0.85). Colors per key via vertex color.

Need per-key color mapping: `_materials` currently returns dict of material name → StandardMaterial3D. Change to also provide `const KEY_COLOR` and `KEY_GROUP`:
```
const MAT_COLOR := {
 "steel": Color(0.54,0.57,0.61), "dark": Color(0.20,0.21,0.24), "bronze": Color(0.70,0.51,0.26),
 "gold": Color(0.92,0.71,0.32), "leather": Color(0.33,0.23,0.15), "wood": Color(0.34,0.23,0.12),
 "skin": Color(0.64,0.49,0.37), "black": Color(0.045,0.045,0.05),
}
```
cloth color depends on team → `_materials` needs team; vertex color for cloth must be team cloth color.

Emissive: `_mat_emit` used for eyes/glow? grep `_mat_emit` usages and keys. Also dragon materials: scale/membrane/horn/eye differing per kind.

This is getting invasive. Alternative: keep material dict but merge groups by creating **one material per group** and add vertex colors during append. Need new `_append` that writes vertex colors: implement by iterating `mesh.surface_get_arrays(0)`:

```
static func _append(sts, mats, key, mesh, xf):
    var group := _GROUP.get(key, "matte")
    var st: SurfaceTool = _ensure(sts, mats, group)
    var col: Color = _COLOR_CACHE[key] (from mats? need color)
    var arrays := mesh.surface_get_arrays(0)
    var verts: PackedVector3Array = arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX]
    var normals: PackedVector3Array = arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL]
    st.set_color(col)
    for i in verts.size():
        st.set_normal((xf.basis * normals[i]).normalized())
        st.add_vertex(xf * verts[i])
    # indices ignored (re-expanding verts, fine)
```
But `mats` dict currently holds materials keyed by material name; `_ensure` uses `mats[key]` as material → with merging, mats needs group→material mapping, and color lookup needs key→color.

Refactor: keep `_materials(team, kind)` returning dict key→Color (albedo), plus metallic/roughness per key? For groups, define group per key; materials per group cached per (group, team?) — metal colors via vertex color; metallic/roughness same for all metal parts; cloth roughness part of matte group but cloth is matte ✓.

Problem: metallic look of bronze/gold vs steel differ only by color; with one metal material metallic 0.5 roughness 0.35, gold looks less shiny — acceptable.

`_tint_team` operates per surface: single metal + single matte surface → 2 surfaces. tint strength 0.3 lerp on material albedo... but albedo now white with vertex color; tint_team duplicates material and sets albedo_color → multiplies vertex colors (vertex_color_use_as_albedo multiplies albedo). Tint by albedo color would tint everything uniformly (both groups) — acceptable-ish, but team tint would multiplicatively shift colors; team color already baked in cloth vertex color, tint on top maybe too strong. Set `tint_strength` meta to 0.15 or reduce.

Risk of visual regression significant. Given user explicitly asked for "材质合并（减少 surface 数）", they accept visual tradeoff? They're a product owner; they asked because I proposed it. But visuals matter (project is about polish). Hmm.

Safer approach preserving colors: **keep per-key materials but merge surfaces that share material**; already one surface per key. Could reduce keys by merging similar keys: steel/dark share metal-ish; but colors differ.

`draw_hero` receives `base` color (team color? Minimap passes `base_col`). HP ring color currently interpolates based on hp. Need: ally → green, enemy → red. We have `base` color which is team-based (red for enemy, blue/green for ally?). Requirement: 我方英雄绿色, 敌方红色 rings.

Call site line 283 in Minimap.gd passes `base_col`. Add parameter `ring_col: Color` to draw_hero, defaulting green? Better compute in Minimap.gd: `ring_col = Color(0.35,1.0,0.5)` if team==player_team else `Color(1.0,0.33,0.3)`; pass to draw_hero.

Also dead state shows number, returns before ring — fine.

Also "小地图中我方英雄头像血量环" — hero avatars drawn by ART.draw_portrait which draws 阵营环 (team ring). Requirement says blood ring unified green/red. So change hp arc color only; keep team ring? The portrait likely draws a colored ring around avatar (team color) — ally blue ring. Requirement: "头像血量环统一为绿色/红色" — the HP ring. Implement ring color by team; keep thickness/alpha.

Also target info panel 质感: find target panel in UI (target_info / target detail panel). Search UI_Manager for "target" drawing.

content.text:
Now design "质感" upgrade of target info panel. Current: flat Panel with border, accent bar, team dot, name, level, HP bar, 4 stat icons+labels. Improvements (minimal-risk, pure visual):

1. **Panel background**: gradient + subtle inner highlight + drop shadow + rounded corners (StyleBoxFlat has bg gradient? Use `StyleBoxFlat` with `bg_color` only; Godot 4.4+ StyleBoxFlat supports `bg_gradient`? In 4.7 there might be `bg_color` only... Actually StyleBoxFlat has no gradient; StyleBoxTexture or a custom drawn Panel via `_draw` needed.)
   Use `UiKit.flat()` helper; improve: increase border alpha, add `shadow_color`/`shadow_size` (StyleBoxFlat supports shadow_size, shadow_color, shadow_offset). That adds depth/质感 cheaply.
2. **Accent bar**: gradient (transparent→team color) - ColorRect can't gradient; use a custom Control with `_draw` or use GradientTexture2D + TextureRect. Simpler: keep ColorRect but add a second thin highlight line below accent (white 12% alpha) and rounded top corners? 
3. **Team dot**: turn into avatar/portrait chip? Add `HeroArt.draw_portrait` for heroes in panel (there is ART in MinimapDraw). Could add a circular avatar in panel — bigger change but high visual payoff. The panel already shows name+level; adding portrait increases質感.
4. **HP bar**: add segmented ticks (每 1000 HP 刻度线), gradient fill, border, and low-HP flash. Also HP bar numeric overlay exists.
5. **Stat rows**: add subtle row separators / rounded background chips behind each attr.

Minimal but impactful, low risk: 
- Panel style: rounded 14, border 2px white 0.22, bg dark blue-grey 0.9, shadow (size 10, alpha 0.35), plus content margin? (StyleBoxFlat content margins don't matter for absolute children).
- Add a **portrait avatar** left of name: use HeroArt portrait when target is Hero (draw via a custom Control drawing portrait). Requires Control subclass drawing; could reuse `MinimapDraw.ART.draw_portrait(ci,...)` in a `_draw` of a custom Control class defined in UI_Manager? Simpler: add class `TargetPortrait extends Control` inside UI_Manager? GDScript inner classes allowed in same file (project already has inner classes like RespawnWidget). Add small inner class that draws portrait + team ring + level badge.
- HP bar: add a second "lag/ghost" color? Could add `hp_lag` visual, but ProgressBar fill only. Add ticks via custom drawn overlay Control.
- Add top gradient accent (GradientTexture2D TextureRect) for sheen.
- Add diagonal gloss highlight overlay Control with `_draw` polygon (white alpha 0.04).

Time-box: implement:
a) panel style upgrade (rounded, shadow, stronger border, slightly larger, add subtle top gloss line).
b) avatar portrait chip for Hero targets (draw via ART) + team ring; hide for non-hero (show team dot fallback / stat icon).
c) HP bar: gradient fill via GradientTexture2D? For ProgressBar fill must be StyleBox; instead build custom HP bar Control with _draw: rounded bg, gradient fill (draw_rect with vertex colors?
